dmp.description:
This project, titled "A Slippery Slope: Understanding Youth Substance Users’ Compliance with Regulatory Policies in Latvia through Behavioral and Cultural Insight," involves comprehensive data collection and analysis to investigate how Latvian youth (aged 16–30) perceive and respond to substance use policies. The data management plan ensures systematic handling of diverse data types collected through mixed methods, including archival policy documents, qualitative interviews, focus groups, and a large-scale quantitative survey.
Data will be collected in multiple phases: policy documents and communication materials will be archived and analyzed qualitatively; semi-structured interviews with policymakers, campaign designers, youth, and frontline workers will be audio-recorded, transcribed, and securely stored; and survey data from 1,000 participants will be collected online using quota sampling to ensure demographic representativeness.
All data will be anonymized to protect participant confidentiality, with informed consent obtained in compliance with GDPR and institutional ethical standards. Qualitative data will be coded and analyzed using software such as NVivo, while quantitative data will be processed with statistical packages like SPSS, Stata, or R. Data integrity and security will be maintained through controlled access and regular backups.
Upon project completion, anonymized datasets and research outputs will be made publicly available on DataverseLV repository, a secure platform for long-term preservation and publication of research data, to support transparency, replication, and secondary data analysis. The data management plan aligns with the project’s interdisciplinary approach, ensuring that data handling supports robust, ethical, and reproducible research outcomes.
